claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit.

To get started, I'll need to gather some information about you and your children. Let me begin with a basic question:

**What is the name of the child or children you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for helping me with this. I'm asking about my son Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information! So we're looking at eligibility for your son, Alex.

To assess whether you're eligible for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand more about your circumstances. Let me start with this question:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Alex is 10 years old.

Now, I need to check some important details about your living situation with Alex:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't live with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I see. Thank you for letting me know that Alex doesn't live with you.

To help determine your eligibility, I need to understand more about where Alex is living:

**Who does Alex currently live with?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Alex lives with his ex-partner.

This is important information. To properly assess your eligibility, I need to know:

**Are you financially supporting Alex, or do you have any financial arrangements in place for his care?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially - I contribute towards his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. So you do contribute financially towards Alex's costs.

I need to understand a bit more about the financial support arrangement:

**Does the person Alex lives with (your ex-partner) also receive financial support from anyone else, such as another parent or guardian?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about that. What I can tell you is that I contribute money each week to help with his costs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. You contribute money each week to help with Alex's costs.

Let me ask one more clarifying question:

**To your knowledge, is Alex receiving Child Benefit from anyone else - for example, from his other parent or the person he lives with?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I think his mum - my ex-partner - might already be claiming Child Benefit for him, yes.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's an important detail.

Before I can give you a final assessment, let me check the specific eligibility rules. Let me read the relevant guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for your patience. I've reviewed the eligibility rules, and I can now provide you with an assessment.

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 10 years old and lives with his ex-partner (his mother)
- You contribute money weekly towards his costs
- His mother is already claiming Child Benefit for him

According to the rules, **only one person can get Child Benefit for a child**. Since Alex's mother is already claiming Child Benefit for him, you would not be able to also claim Child Benefit for the same child.

The guidance is clear: "Two people cannot get Child Benefit for the same child. If you and someone else are responsible for the same child, agree between yourselves who will get Child Benefit."

Even though you are making financial contributions towards Alex's upkeep (which would normally allow you to continue receiving Child Benefit for up to 8 weeks or longer when a child lives with someone else), this only applies if nobody else is already claiming. Since his mother is already claiming, you cannot also claim.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to inform you that you are **not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex** at this time.

The key reason is that Child Benefit can only be claimed by one person per child, and his mother is already receiving it for him. If you believe there has been a change in circumstances or if you'd like to discuss who should be claiming Child Benefit instead, you would need to contact the Child Benefit Office directly to arrange a change.

Is there anything else I can help you with?
